HAND-AUTHORED, NOT RECORDED. Read this before trusting these files.

No LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY / LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY exists on the machine that
created this package, so no live exchange produced these files. They are
hand-authored against the documented Langfuse REST schema as of 2026-08-29
(the generated OpenAPI at https://api.langfuse.com/swagger.json):

  - Dataset resolution: GET {host}/api/public/v2/datasets/{datasetName},
    response is the dataset object itself: id, name, projectId, createdAt,
    updatedAt. An unknown name is 404.
  - Dataset items:     GET {host}/api/public/dataset-items?datasetName=
    <name>&page=<n>&limit=100, response envelope {data: [...], meta:
    {page, limit, totalItems, totalPages}} — page-numbered, not cursor-based.
    Each item carries id, datasetId, input (JSON, nullable), expectedOutput
    (JSON, nullable), metadata, sourceObservationId, sourceTraceId, status
    (ACTIVE | ARCHIVED), createdAt, updatedAt.
  - Auth: HTTP basic auth, public key as user and secret key as password,
    per Langfuse's API documentation.

The schemas are versioned and can change — that is the adapter's accepted
drift risk, recorded in docs/plans/2026-08-29-langfuse-evals-adapter.md.

Until a real exchange replaces them, the adapter rests on a documentation
claim rather than on evidence. When LANGFUSE keys exist, re-record:

  make record-fixtures

(or directly: KNO_LIVE_TESTS=1 KNO_RECORD_FIXTURES=1 go test -tags=integration
  ./adapters/evals/langfuse/ -run TestRecordLiveFixtures)

which captures the live dataset and its first items page into testdata/live/
(and refuses to record a response that echoes a key). Those captures are the
evidence to review against these files. The malformed, empty, duplicate,
null-input, and archived fixtures cannot be recorded — no live dataset is
malformed — so they stay hand-authored and are judged against the captures.

What each fixture is for:

  dataset-support-llm.json   name resolution; one dataset, updatedAt
                            "2026-08-01T12:00:00Z", 4 items across 2 pages
  items-llm-page1.json      first page (2 rows: an escape/unicode row and a
                            nested-key-order row), meta totalPages 2
  items-llm-page2.json      page 2 (a key-unsorted input whose canonical JSON
                            the goldens pin, and a null expectedOutput ->
                            empty Expected); last page
  items-empty.json          a dataset that exists with no items -> zero Cases
  items-duplicate.json      the same item id twice -> fatal naming the id
                            (the torn-page story: a dataset edited under the
                            pagination)
  items-archived.json       one ARCHIVED row (client-side filter) and one
                            ACTIVE row
  items-derived.json        sourceObservationId and sourceTraceId rows ->
                            Provenance.Derived; one authored row -> not
  items-null-input.json     an item whose input is null -> fatal
  items-message-array.json  an item whose input is a messages array -> raw
                            canonical JSON as the prompt (plan F7)
  golden/canonical.json     the pinned canonical-JSON encoding: key order,
                            HTML escaping, and unicode behavior
